Ordnance 0.4.1. A clean break from the DDMM era.

## What Ordnance does

**Import from your current mod manager.** One-click import from **HD2 Arsenal** and **Echelon** — plus the older HD2 mod manager, Vortex, and your Downloads folder. It reads each manager's own records (Arsenal's `hd2a_data.json`, Echelon's `library.json`) and brings mods over with their names, on/off state, and options intact.

**Automatic update checking and downloading.** Ordnance checks every mod against its source — **AyakaMods, GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and Nexus Mods** — and tells you what's outdated. For sites with public downloads (GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop), a **one-click update downloads and installs the new file in place**, keeping the same mod ID and profile settings. Auto-checks run on startup and on a configurable interval (opt-in). Nexus Mods updates go through your browser, using your personal API key.

**One sealed swap.** All enabled mods merge into a single, conflict-resolved `.dl_bin` file set, with a merged boot script and loader-conflict detection — no loose files, no load-order guessing.

**Profiles and categories.** Switch between profiles in the sidebar, group mods into categories, and keep each mod's version visible at a glance.

**Browser extension.** The `ordnance-extension` (Chrome/Firefox) adds an **Install with Ordnance** button on AyakaMods, Nexus Mods, ModWorkshop, GameBanana, and GitHub mod pages.

## What's new in 0.4.1

- **Complete rebrand to Ordnance.** The last `ddmm`/`Democracy Defender` remnants are gone — crate name, identifiers, data folder, native-messaging host, keyring service, extension namespace and Gecko ID, CSS classes, environment variables, docs, and package names are all `Ordnance`. **On first launch, existing data migrates automatically** from the old folder to `com.cavadus.ordnance` — mods, profiles, settings, and images all carry over.
- **MIT license**, with attribution to the Apache-2.0 upstream projects it derives from (teutinsa's HD2MM, katsyk's Democracy Defender) retained.
- **Self-describing stat-plans.** The `.dl_bin` applier no longer hardcodes game-table layout — stat-plan files carry their own layout metadata, and table layouts live author-side in `hd2-mods/tools/statplan_layout.py`.
- **Sealed-box keys shipped in the build**, so a fresh install works out of the box with no setup.
- **Dependency hygiene** — `tokio` 1.53.3 clears `RUSTSEC-2026-0386`.

## Which file do I download?

| You want... | Download |
| --- | --- |
| A normal install on Windows | `Ordnance-0.4.1-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows, unzip and run | `Ordnance-0.4.1-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux: Fedora, Nobara, openSUSE | `Ordnance-0.4.1-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint | `Ordnance-0.4.1-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `Ordnance-0.4.1-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

**Browser extension:** `ordnance-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip` or `ordnance-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip`. Load it unpacked. The button says Install with Ordnance.
